The m118 intermediate point was close to measured V1/V2, and the m159 and m114 curve points were also reasonably centered, showing that targeted interpolation can repair some regimes. In contrast, m104 matched loading points both measured near 5/13 ml while the model predicted about 14/35 ml, showing that loading corrections are scaffold-specific rather than a uniform mass shift. The m177 high-ratio point confirmed a real long V2 tail, while m144, m98, m11, m85, and m74 showed that broad predictions can also substantially overstate the finish. The next batch therefore combines matched loading points with transition-zone curves, direct V2-tail probes, molecule-novel transfer controls, and ordinary calibration anchors.","batch_rationale":"The batch concentrates local curves where measured data show sharp or irregular condition response: m206, m119, m207, m141, m205, m90, m125, m114, m160, m161, m72, m118, m177, m98, m164, m129, m31, and m198. Several pairs vary loading at a fixed molecule and mobile phase so the retrained model can separate mass and loading-solvent effects from solvent-strength effects. The m177, m125, m141, m198, and m98 selections directly target V2-tail calibration, while m95 and m47 provide molecule-novel chemical transfer labels. The m203 control and other compact points test whether tail repairs preserve ordinary-row calibration. Together these labels cover failure repair, nonlinear scaffold-condition boundaries, loading interactions, chemical novelty, and centered controls across the Row-distribution."}
